newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke says Brown's is "tightening" budget.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke says Brown's is "tightening" budget.

text.p: Former Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke on Wednesday summarised the budget of his Labour successor Gordon Brown as a tightening of policy which would slow the economy down over the next year.
"This is a big tightening of policy budget," Clarke told the BBC.
"He hasn't hit the ordinary voter too much. He hasn't hit consumer taxes in any very unexpected way...he has hit the corporate sector."
Asked what he thought the effect of the budget would be in a year's time, Clarke said: "slowing down the economy."
"He is trying to get a free lunch out of the windfall tax, he's gone for the biggest possible hit on that," added Clarke, who was ousted in the May 1 election.

Although he praised Brown's plan to put some of the money from the windfall tax on utilities into education, Brown added: "I fear the welfare-to-work programme won't produce what they claim." -- London newsroom **4471 542 7947
